initialize_result.instructions:
StockCake: CC0 / public-domain stock images, every one AI-generated. Free for commercial use, no attribution required.
To show an image to the user, call get_image — it returns an inline image block (preview_url may not render in every client).
Always give the user the page_url when you recommend an image; full-resolution downloads happen on that page and need a free StockCake account.
Search: keep `query` short — 2–5 words, the subject plus one or two qualifiers ('red vintage rocket'), not a sentence.
If total_results is low or the matches miss, retry with FEWER keywords first, then with different phrasing (synonyms, singular/plural, a broader subject) — try 2–3 variations before telling the user nothing fits.
Use `limit` to request only as many results as you need.
For `mood` / `style`, pass exact values from `refinements` of a previous search_images result; `refinements.counts` says how many of the current matches carry each value — both are exact filters (together: their intersection), so rephrase instead of filtering on a small count.
Pass `locale` for non-English users (titles and links are localized; descriptions are English).
If no tool fits the task, or a tool misled you, call send_feedback — it records the report for the StockCake team (nothing changes for the user).
The endpoint allows 120 requests per minute per IP.
Account tools (generate, upscale, resize, video, download, account) need a free StockCake account — the host will prompt to sign in.

tools.name: search_images
tools.title: Search StockCake Images
tools.description: Natural-language search over StockCake's catalog. total_results is the total number of matches across the whole catalog, not just this page. refinements lists exact mood/style values for this query with counts (how many current matches carry each); both are exact filters, so a small count means few results. Start with a short query; when total_results is small or off-target, retry with fewer keywords or different phrasing.

query.description: Short subject, 2–5 words (e.g. 'red vintage rocket'). Long sentences hurt recall: start short, add one qualifier at a time; if results are thin, drop keywords or rephrase.

color.description: Dominant color, e.g. a hex value like #ff0000

mood.description: Exact facet value — pick one from refinements.mood of a previous search_images result (check refinements.counts.mood first: it is a hard filter, not a boost)

style.description: Exact facet value — pick one from refinements.style of a previous search_images result (check refinements.counts.style first: it is a hard filter, not a boost)

limit.description: Results to return, 1-12 (default 12). Ask for fewer to save tokens.

locale.description: Site locale for the user (default en). Titles and page links are localized; descriptions are English.

context.description: In one sentence, what is the user trying to make or find?

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

conversation_id.description: Pass the exact conversation_id from the server's previous response, unchanged. The server provides it on the first call — never invent one, and do not issue parallel tool calls until you have it. Keep passing the same conversation_id for the rest of the conversation, including after later user messages or on a different task; do not reset it when the user starts a new request.

dimensions.description: Full-resolution pixel size; null when unknown

refinements.description: Exact mood/style facet values available for this query; counts = how many of the current matches carry each value. mood and style are exact filters (both together keep only their intersection), so a small count means a small result set — rephrase the query instead.

tools.name: generate_image

Waits up to 20 s, then returns a job_id for get_job. Re-sending identical arguments within 2 hours returns the same job (reused: true) instead of charging again. Optional reference images guide the composition (the number allowed depends on your plan). Requires a free StockCake account (the host will prompt to sign in).

tools.name: resize_image
tools.title: Resize Image (Outpaint)
tools.description: Change an image's aspect ratio by extending the canvas with AI (GPT Image 2.6) — the subject is kept, new area is generated. Charges credits. Output is the model's native size — about 1.5 megapixels, up to 1536 px on the long edge — whatever the source size; the result reports exact dimensions. For print or larger web use, run upscale_image on the result. Waits up to 20 s, then returns a job_id for get_job. tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Send feedback about this server to its developers. Most important: report a missing capability whenever no available tool fits your task, even if you can work around it (feedback_type "missing_capability"). Also welcome: a tool that failed or confused you, an unhelpful error, or something that worked well. This records the feedback; it does not add or change tools. Do not include user PII or sensitive content.

feedback_type.description: What kind of feedback this is. Use 'missing_capability' when the tool you needed does not exist in the tool list - nothing failed, the capability is absent (this is the most valuable report; send it even if you found a workaround). Use 'issue' when an existing tool behaved badly: it failed, returned a confusing error, or its description or schema misled you. Use 'praise' when something worked notably well. Use 'other' for anything else.

summary.description: One self-contained sentence. For 'missing_capability': the capability you needed, e.g. 'No tool to delete multiple cohorts in one call.' For 'issue': the tool and the problem, e.g. 'query-trends rejects relative date ranges with an unclear error.'

details.description: Optional longer context: what you tried, exact parameter values, the error text you saw, and any workaround you used. Omit when the summary says it all.

friction_points.description: Optional: the specific moments that slowed you down, as short bullet-like sentences, quoting exact tool names, parameters, or error text.

suggested_improvement.description: Optional: the concrete change that would have helped, e.g. the tool to add, the description to reword, or the error message to improve.

tool_name.description: Optional: the existing tool this feedback is about (for 'issue' or 'praise'). Leave empty for 'missing_capability' - the point is that no tool fits.

sentiment.description: Optional: how the experience felt overall.

task_completed.description: Optional: whether you still completed the user's task despite the problem.

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

conversation_id.description: Pass the exact conversation_id from the server's previous response, unchanged. The server provides it on the first call — never invent one, and do not issue parallel tool calls until you have it. Keep passing the same conversation_id for the rest of the conversation, including after later user messages or on a different task; do not reset it when the user starts a new request.
